subject: Transient p99 amplification — prefetch/fanout impact & customer-facing status update
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Rogers <jamie.rogers@lakeshore.ai>; support@lakeshore.ai
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-30T08:12:00Z
Subject: Transient p99 amplification — early notice and status

Hi Jamie / Lakeshore team,

Wanted to let you know we observed a transient amplification in p99 request latency across a prefetch + fanout workload affecting a subset of hosted inference routes that serve your test and canary traffic. Impact window so far: ~08:05–08:40 UTC. Symptoms: elevated p99 (up to ~3.2x baseline), some user requests hitting client-side timeouts at 5s (your SDK default). No full request failures at infra layer; many requests completed but with elongated tails.

What we're doing now (first response):
- Enabled a temporary fallback routing to a smaller-configuration model variant to reduce tail latency for inflight requests.
- Adjusted prefetch concurrency and limited aggressive fanout for the affected tenant pools.
- Captured KV-cache and prefetch traces; attaching a short incident snippet for your engineering review (incident-snippet-0530.jsonl).

Immediate ask: can you confirm if you saw any client errors (timeouts / 5xx) beyond 08:40 UTC, and whether there were any customer-visible drops in throughput on your side? That will help us scope the postmortem and any credits discussion.

We will follow up with a clearer root-cause note within 4 hours and a postmortem doc link. Apologies for the disruption — we're treating this as high priority.

— Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Customer Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference

Thanks Evelyn — we did see an uptick in client timeouts in our observability around 08:10–08:35 UTC for our staging traffic (we route canaries through your hosted endpoints). Two quick notes:

- No production customer impact reported yet, but our monitoring is noisy and we'd like the exact list of affected route ids so we can correlate.

Appreciate the quick mitigation work. Please include the route ids and any L7 traces you captured.

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-30T09:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Transient p99 amplification — early notice and status

Jamie — thanks for confirming. Quick follow-up with the route ids and what we found:

Affected routes (sample):
- route-usa-west-3: /v1/generate (tenant pool: lakeshore-staging-1)
- route-usa-west-3-prefetch: background prefetch shard for lakeshore-staging-1

Preliminary observations:
- Trigger: concurrent prefetch fanout increased beyond expected distribution (a customer-side workload pattern amplified prefetch concurrency while demand to the same KV-cache hot keys spiked). This caused transient contention on the local prefetch worker pools and increased per-request queueing.
- Impact: elevated p99 (tail) as requests waited behind long prefetch tasks; most requests still completed but with tail latency. No token-level corruption or data leakage observed.

Mitigations applied (summary):
- Reduced prefetch fanout parallelism from 12->4 for the affected shard (prefetch-config-diff.txt attached).
- Enabled quick-fallback routing: inflight requests that hit prefetch queue depth > threshold now route to a compact model variant with faster latency at slightly higher token cost.
- Elevated logging for a 1-hour window to capture KV-cache contention and per-worker queue lengths; pushed anonymized traces to the Drive folder (link below).

Next steps (we'll own these):
1) Full postmortem and timeline with root cause and long-term fix options (shard-level backpressure, prefetch backoff, fanout smoothing). Target ETA: EOD PT.
2) Action items: limit prefetch fanout by tenant, add adaptive prefetch backoff, and increase prefetch worker headroom for hotspot keys.

No change to data residency or durability was detected. I'll populate the postmortem doc and invite Lakeshore SREs to review.

Attachments: prefetch-config-diff.txt, incident-snippet-0530.jsonl
Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/incident-0530-prefetch-analysis

— Evelyn
Customer Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference

Evelyn / Sean — good quick work on the mitigation. Two internal action items I want to confirm before we finalize the customer postmortem:
1) Credits/compensation: Product needs a short impact statement with exact window and estimated affected QPS to scope any goodwill credit. Can you confirm the impacted window as 08:05–08:40 UTC and estimated affected p95/p99 QPS for lakeshore-staging-1?
2) Postmortem review: schedule 60m review with Engineering + SRE + Product next Tue 2026-06-02 16:00 UTC. I'll own the invite and the doc (Drive link above).

Also, for the customer-facing status note I propose we keep it concise: cause (prefetch fanout + KV hot key contention), mitigation (fallback routing + reduced fanout), and next steps (postmortem + fixes). Marissa -> please draft the final statuspage blurb after Evelyn populates timeline.

— Marissa
